AbstractText.Label: RATIONALE
AbstractText.content: Osteosarcoma is the most common malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents. Metastasis occurs early, the mortality rate is high, and the tumor results in a tremendous physical, mental, and economic burden on patients. Therefore, the treatment of osteosarcoma has been important for orthopedic surgeons. However, treatment has always been a difficult problem globally.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENT CONCERN
AbstractText.content: We present the case of a 22-year-old girl with increasing local pain in the distal left thigh.

AbstractText.Label: DIAGNOSES
AbstractText.content: The patient was initially diagnosed as bone cancer according to computed tomography (CT) and X-ray imaging. And the patient was further diagnosed as osteosarcoma via to puncture biopsy of the left distal femur.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: Local arterial infusion chemotherapy, systemic intravenous chemotherapy, and curettage was conducted because of limb salvage program.

AbstractText.Label: OUTCOMES
AbstractText.content: The patient was doing well with no evidence of local or distant recurrence 7 years after the surgery.

AbstractText.Label: LESSONS
AbstractText.content: Our case indicated that limb osteosarcoma patients can undergo a limb salvage program of local arterial infusion chemotherapy, systemic intravenous chemotherapy, and curettage.

Article.ArticleTitle: Therapeutic effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with curettage to treat distal femoral osteosarcoma: A case report.
